verdictBasis: 0 blockers, 2 SHOULD-FIX, 2 advisories. ACCEPT was gated at 0 blockers AND 0 SHOULD-FIX.
verdictStatement: Both v8 blockers are closed. The filesystem target now has a designated input rather than a property: targetPath is the signed closure's install root, declared an immutable preselection value bound in the signed profile or carrier and expressly not derived from later object resolutions, with its own failure clause. The Linux observation names the verifier process, reads /proc/<verifierPid>/mountinfo when the observer is independent, and requires later resolvers to stay in that mount namespace or refuse. companionObservation is now a real retainedEventSchema field with explicit optionality, a closed four-field shape, an explicit not-nested-under-taggedEvidenceForm rule, and /loaderTraces added to the roster — the correct pattern, applied fully. reMeasurementAtV6 and V8 are demoted to HISTORICAL, exactly one block carries standing LIVE, and its three values all reproduce against live bytes at the dispatched HEAD. The duplicated rotation sentence is gone. What remains are two second-order gaps inside the new text. The designated path has two conflicting resolution rules — derivation resolves it, the Linux record selection string-matches it — and 'ordinary host path resolution' is the one loose phrase in an otherwise exact block, where PTCB-V8-B1 asked for exact path-resolution rules. And the verifier identity that the namespace rule depends on is said to be recorded on the profile, which has no field for it and could not hold a per-run value in a frozen key, while the retained event schema that gained companionObservation this generation gained no namespace evidence.

shouldFix.title: targetPath carries two conflicting resolution rules, and the resolution itself is the one unspecified step in the block

measurement.derivationResolves: targetPath.derivation reads 'The target volume is the volume that contains that path after ordinary host path resolution of the install root.'
measurement.linuxDoesNot: linux.recordSelection reads 'the record whose mount-point field is the longest prefix of targetPath'. That is a string comparison against the designated path as written, not against a resolved path. If any component of the install root is a symbolic link crossing into another mount, the longest mount-point prefix of the literal path and the mount containing the resolved path are different records with different fs_vfstype tokens.
measurement.macosImplicitlyResolves: macos.interface passes targetPath to statfs, which follows symbolic links, so the macOS branch reports the volume of the resolved path. The two osFamily branches therefore apply different resolution semantics to the same designated input, which the shared derivation clause does not reconcile.
measurement.theLoosePhrase: 'ordinary host path resolution' is undefined: it does not say whether symbolic links are followed, whether the path is canonicalised as realpath(3) would, or how bind mounts are treated. Everything around it is exact — Unicode NFC, ASCII case-fold, U+003A, longest prefix, last in file order, first field after the '-' separator — which makes this the single unspecified step in an otherwise closed algorithm.

shouldFix.againstTheFrozenRequirement: PTCB-V8-B1's requiredRepair asked for 'a canonical installation/executable root with exact path-resolution rules'. The canonical root is delivered and is the substance of the blocker; the exact path-resolution rules are not.
shouldFix.consequence: Two conforming Linux verifiers on one host — one following derivation, one following recordSelection literally — compute different filesystem members for the same designated install root whenever it traverses a symlink across a mount, which container and package-manager layouts routinely produce. Fail-closed rather than exploitable, since a mismatch refuses, but the required member is not yet reproducible for those hosts.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: State the resolution once, in targetPath, and have both branches consume its output: for example that targetPath is canonicalised by resolving every symbolic link component before measurement, that the canonical path is the input to statfs on macOS and to the mount-point prefix match on Linux, and that a path that cannot be canonicalised refuses. Then delete 'ordinary host path resolution' or define it as that canonicalisation.

shouldFix.title: The verifier identity the namespace rule depends on is recorded nowhere, and the namespace MUST has no retained evidence

measurement.theClaim: observerProcess reads 'The verifier process that performs preselection observation. Its process identity is recorded on the profile.' namespace reads 'the named verifier process's mount namespace at preselection. Later resolvers MUST remain in that same namespace or the profile refuses.'
measurement.noFieldOnTheProfile: selectorGrammar.requiredMembers is byte-identical to v8 and remains exactly osFamily, architecture, supportedVersionOrBuildSelector and filesystemWhereItAffectsResolution. No profile field holds a verifier process identity, and the token verifierPid occurs only inside this block's own prose and honestyRepairsFromV8.
measurement.andItCouldNotHoldOne: A profile key is frozen and reused across runs — beforeAllowlistFreeze and the whole allowlist model depend on that. A verifier process identity is per-run. Recording it on the profile would either make the frozen key run-specific or mean nothing across runs, so the recording site named is not merely missing but the wrong kind of place.
measurement.noRetainedEvidence: retainedEventSchema was edited this generation and now carries fifteen fields including the new companionObservation, but none of them is a mount-namespace identity. processIdentityAndParentage records process identity, not the namespace. So a MUST that later resolvers remain in the preselection namespace cannot be checked against a retained qualification trace after the fact.
measurement.theArtifactKnowsThePattern: This is the shape I raised at CLAUDE-V8-S1 and Codex raised at PTCB-V8-S1 — a claim routed to a location that does not exist — and v9 fixed that instance correctly by adding the field to retainedEventSchema, giving it a closed shape, and putting /loaderTraces on the roster. The same pattern is not applied here.

shouldFix.consequence: The namespace constraint is stated as a refusal condition but is neither storable at preselection nor auditable from the trace, so two verifiers can both claim conformance while only one actually held the constraint, and G22 evidence cannot settle it.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Name the real recording site. Record the verifier process and its mount-namespace identity on the qualification run rather than on the frozen profile, and add a namespace identity field to retainedEventSchema alongside companionObservation so the MUST has evidence. If the intent is that the profile records only that a namespace binding was required, say that instead of 'its process identity is recorded on the profile'.

coordinatorNote: Both blockers are genuinely closed and the fixes are structural rather than verbal. The filesystem target now has a signed, immutable, designated input instead of a self-referential property, which was the whole substance of PTCB-V8-B1 and of my own B-1; the Linux observer and namespace binding answer Codex's second element point by point; companionObservation is provisioned exactly the way it should have been at v8, with the field, a closed shape, an explicit not-nested rule and /loaderTraces put on the roster; and the remeasurement standing scheme is not only completed but generalised into a rule that forecloses demoting a block off-roster. What I am left with are two second-order gaps that both sit inside the new text. The designated path is resolved by one clause and string-matched by another, so a single install root traversing a symlink across a mount yields two lawful answers on Linux, and 'ordinary host path resolution' is the only loose phrase left in a block that is otherwise exact to the code point — where PTCB-V8-B1 asked specifically for exact path-resolution rules. And the verifier identity on which the new namespace refusal depends is said to be recorded on the profile, which has no field for it and, being frozen and reused, is the wrong kind of place for a per-run value, while the retained event schema that gained a field this generation gained no namespace evidence, so the MUST cannot be audited from a qualification trace. Both are fail-closed and neither touches authority. The two advisories are small: the newest ledger round is stored under the unqualified ids that idCollisionNote exists to disambiguate, and one historical note repeats a word. DR-126 stays OPEN, no row of any number is marked SATISFIED, all three D-096 occurrences are prohibitions, no per-OS table is populated, and nothing here qualifies G22 or authorizes docs/v2/implementation/. The subject, prompt, file 08 and COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md were not edited and nothing was committed.
